bugs: GET /api/posts?status=&tag= returns 422 because the IndexPostRequest rules (app/Http/Requests/IndexPostRequest.php:14-16) are not nullable. Empty query params become null and then fail the enum/string rules, so clients can't send a blank filter.

Tag::firstOrCreate in app/Models/Post.php:55 is not race-safe against the unique tags.name index. Two concurrent requests that create the same new tag can throw a unique-constraint QueryException. createOrFirst exists for exactly this case.
antipatterns: app/Http/Requests/UpdatePostRequest.php:13-19 copies the StorePostRequest rules almost line for line instead of reusing them, so status/tags rules can drift apart
app/Http/Requests/StorePostRequest.php:17-18 has no max on the tags array and no distinct rule, so the request can carry any number of tags
app/Models/Post.php:61-70 scopes take nullable args and wrap their body in when(). Optional-filter logic is pushed into the model, and the scopes can't be reused cleanly as required filters
app/Policies/PostPolicy.php:17 delete() repeats the update() logic instead of delegating to it
app/Http/Controllers/PostController.php:18 uses with('tags') to load full tag rows when only the name is used
strengths: Very thin controller: user()->posts() scoping, safe()->except('tags'), and paginate()->withQueryString()
Authorisation via ->can() route middleware means a non-author gets 403 before validation runs, and a test covers this
Uses modern attributes (#[Fillable], #[ObservedBy], #[Scope]), a backed enum cast, and Rule::enum
Unique-slug generation lives in an observer with an empty-slug fallback; published_at is set in saving()
The routes file is compact and readable
Tests use hasAttached factories, freezeSecond, and assertModelMissing, and include a test that the tag filter doesn't leak other users' posts

antipatterns: routes/api.php:7-12 mixes apiResource()->only(['index','store']) with a separate controller group for update/destroy. This is more ceremony than one prefix/controller group or apiResource()->except('show') with authorisation
app/Http/Requests/StorePostRequest.php:25-28 adds a postData() wrapper that is just safe()->except('tags'), a thin layer with little value
app/Http/Requests/IndexPostRequest.php:22 coerces with tryFrom((string) ...) on a value that is already validated; $this->enum('status', PostStatus::class) would be the idiomatic accessor
Tag dedupe is case-sensitive ('PHP' and 'php' become separate tags). This is a minor design choice that the code doesn't document
strengths: Route-model binding by slug (getRouteKeyName), which fits a unique slug column
Tag::createOrFirst is race-safe against the unique tags.name index
UpdatePostRequest extends StorePostRequest and overrides only title/body with spread syntax (DRY). Tags get max:20 and distinct
Index filters are nullable, so empty query params are ignored instead of returning 422. A test covers this
The controller uses when() with non-nullable #[Scope] methods, so the scopes stay clean and reusable. Eager loading selects only tags:id,name
Composite index (user_id, status, created_at) matches the index query
Policy delete() delegates to update(); 403 comes from ->can() middleware before validation

Thorough tests: slug stays the same when the title changes, guest gets 401 without an Accept header, duplicate/empty tags, combined filters, pagination defaults, and that clients can't set slug, owner or published_at

v.rationale:
I ranked impl-2 first (8.6) and impl-1 second (7.8). Both suites pass: 31 tests for impl-2, 30 for impl-1.

The two implementations are nearly the same design: an enum cast, an observer for the unique slug and published_at, a policy enforced through ->can() route middleware, form requests, a resource that plucks tag names, and user()->posts() scoping. Both meet every requirement.

My probes covered six edge cases on each. Both handle these the same way: un-publishing and re-publishing keeps the original published_at, a guest request without JSON headers gets 401, and null fields or non-string tags get 422.

They differ in a few places:
- **Empty filters:** `?status=&tag=` returns 422 in impl-1 because its index rules aren't nullable. impl-2 ignores blank filters and has a test for it.
- **Tag creation:** impl-1 uses firstOrCreate, which can race against the unique tag-name index. impl-2 uses createOrFirst, which is safe.
- **Rule duplication:** impl-1 copies the store rules into UpdatePostRequest. impl-2 extends StorePostRequest and overrides only title and body.
- **Tag limits:** impl-2 caps tags at 20 and adds a distinct rule; impl-1 has neither.
- **Other idioms:** impl-2 binds routes by slug, loads only tag id and name, and keeps its scopes non-nullable, putting the optional-filter logic in when() in the controller.

impl-2 has a few weaknesses of its own. Its routes file splits apiResource() and a separate group, which is clumsier than impl-1's single group. Its postData() wrapper adds little.

Neither has a serious bug. impl-2 wins on robustness and on how it uses Laravel's idioms.
